newsitem.title: USA: Rochester Medical device cleared for trial.
newsitem.headline: Rochester Medical device cleared for trial.

text.p: Rochester Medical Corp said on Wednesday it had received Food and Drug Administration approval to begin clinical studies of the FemSoft urethral insert for managing female stress incontinence.
The studies will be conducted over the coming months at nationally recognized medical institutions, the company said.
Results will be submitted to the FDA for a Premarket Approval Application.
The FemSoft device is a soft, fluid-filled insert that assists weakened muscles. It requires no inflation, deflation, syringes or valving mechanisms, the company said.

"We are optimistic that these studies will provide the clinical data necessary to demonstrate the safety and effectiveness of the FemSoft device in extended use by a significant patient population," said company President Anthony Conway.
